video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] Watching cold, I can only make out a rough story. A giant scorpion fights three tree creatures, then the trees are pushed up by spikes from the ground and disappear, leaving the scorpion alone. Several key beats are unclear. (1) Who attacks whom: in the 1.5s–4.75s cells, the scorpion's legs and tail tangle with all three tree creatures. They overlap heavily, and no single cell shows who hit whom. It reads as a messy brawl, not a clear skill. (2) Who casts the skill: at 5.0s–5.25s the scorpion seems to burrow, leaving only its tail above ground. At 5.5s–5.75s it is completely gone, and the frame shows just the three tree creatures standing. At 6.0s–6.75s brown-black spike columns rise from the ground under the trees, but the scorpion is nowhere in frame. A first-time viewer can't tell whether the scorpion caused this or it is an environmental hazard or the trees' own skill. At 7.0s a scorpion pops up at the bottom right, but it looks much smaller than the giant one in the 0s–4.75s foreground. That size jump is so big I'm not sure it's the same creature. (3) Hit and result: from 6.25s to 7.25s the trees are lifted to the top of the spike columns. By 7.5s–7.75s they have simply vanished into dust, with no clear frame of them being hit, falling or breaking apart. From 8.0s on there is only some debris on the ground, so I can't tell whether they died or were just knocked away. (4) Spectacle: the skill effect at 6.0s–7.25s is brown-grey earth spikes and dust in the same colours as the background. There's no highlight or contrasting colour, so it does not meet the Vision goals of 'skills look more spectacular' and 'outcome is visible.'
